meta_description: Done-for-you release operations for B2B SaaS teams that want customer-facing launches without docs, support, and rollout chaos.
for_whom: For 5-100 person B2B SaaS teams shipping customer-facing releases
hero_headline: Ship customer-facing releases without the docs, support, and rollout scramble
hero_subheadline: We turn every launch into a clean release packet: docs delta, internal enablement brief, rollout notes, and a first-week issue digest.
secondary_cta_text: See a redacted sample launch packet
credibility_line: NDA-friendly. Least-privilege access. One product line at a time. You approve customer-facing copy before it goes live.
pain_paragraph: Most launch pain starts after engineering says the feature is done. Docs are stale, support finds out too late, customer success has no rollout notes, and sales keeps showing the old workflow. The result is confused customers, avoidable tickets, and senior people doing launch cleanup at the worst possible moment.
before: Docs updates happen at the last minute or not at all
Support learns about the release from confused customers
Sales and CS use stale screenshots, notes, or demos
Known issues and rollout risks live in Slack threads
after: A clear launch packet for every customer-facing release
Docs delta tracked before launch day
Support macros and known-issue notes ready in advance
A first-week digest showing adoption friction and launch issues
offer_summary: ReleaseReady Desk is a done-for-you release-operations layer for one product line. We keep launches customer-ready with a concrete checklist, release brief, docs-delta tracker, support prep, rollout copy, and a first-week follow-through digest.
included: Launch intake + release checklist for one product line
Docs-delta tracker with exact pages/assets to update
Internal release brief for support, CS, and sales
Support macro pack + known-issue / workaround notes
Draft changelog and rollout/customer announcement copy
First-week issue + adoption digest after launch
excluded: Full product marketing strategy or sales enablement overhaul
Net-new documentation projects beyond agreed page/asset limits
Running customer webinars, demos, or live training sessions
process: 15-min fit call to confirm release cadence, ICP, and systems
Onboarding: gather current docs, release workflow, owners, and templates
For each release: intake the change, build the launch packet, route approvals, and prep support/CS
After launch: capture first-week issues, adoption friction, and recommended fixes in one digest
pricing_details: Starter tier covers one product line, up to 2 customer-facing releases per month, one docs-delta tracker per release, and one first-week digest. Heavier release volume or direct docs editing is scoped separately.
guarantee_line: Pilot offer: $500 for a release readiness audit + one sample launch packet, credited toward month one if we keep going.

faq.a: Usually read/write access to your docs workspace, a release tracker, and a place to draft support/customer-facing notes. No production access needed. We work with least-privilege access and can use an NDA.

faq.q: What needs to be true for this to work?
faq.a: You need one named internal owner, a rough release calendar, and a product contact who can answer edge-case questions quickly. This works best when releases already have some planning, but the execution layer is messy.
Usually 3-5 business days to learn your workflow, collect current docs/templates, and set up the launch packet format. After that, new releases follow the same system.

faq.q: How do you handle retention and sensitive information?
faq.a: We keep only the working documents needed for active releases, follow your retention window when possible, and can delete drafts/artifacts on request after handoff.

faq.q: Will you rewrite our whole docs site?
faq.a: No. The core offer is release operations, not a blank-check docs project. We define clear page/asset limits and flag larger docs work separately before it expands scope.

trust_basics_line: One promise: cleaner customer-facing releases. One CTA. Clear scope boundaries. Instrument pageview → CTA click → booked call from day one.
